summary: Run 39837319401 of wasm-custody-pilot.yml was the single dispatch admitted by FS-GG/.github#4710 comment 6347853904, at 1638416 (artifact zip sha256 c80e5a9a..., 88 files including hidden ones). Independent acceptance (comment 6349235037): ACCEPTED WITH GAPS. Established on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04, consistent across runner builds 20261021.345.10 (run 1) and 20261018.339.1 (run 2), with the pinned managed-group owner d846dbe1: all 20 groups contained and observed-empty-removed, and the systemd unit properties captured with systemctl show (TasksMax=4096, MemoryMax=8589934592, RuntimeMaxUSec=30min, Delegate, NoNewPrivileges, KillMode=control-group) matching the admission. For Chromium headless-shell 1243 and Firefox 1543, the owner retired survivors: a detached holder kept 6 or 7 browser processes alive 2 s after the leader exited; they were recorded as residual and retired by SIGTERM and then cgroup.kill (populatedAfter=false). Clean stock shutdown and deadline retirement repeated. Gaps: the admitted WebKit apt install (51 pinned packages, resolving to 176 and 95 MB) fetched only 30 packages from the Azure mirror before the step's 5-minute timeout and unpacked nothing, so WebKit still lacked 34 host libraries. The pilot mislabelled this as not-attempted, because the step never wrote its exit codes or after-snapshot, and apt termination after the timeout was not shown. Forced cases show observed browser members, not those alive at the deadline. Lessons: bound each apt call itself and write the evidence in a trap; derive state from explicit step markers, not from missing files. A third, final run is admitted (comment 6349235037).
title: Second WASM custody pilot run established owner survivor retirement for Chromium and Firefox; WebKit install timed out
